- The maximum number of playlists any single track appears in is 5 playlists.
- There are 41 distinct tracks that each appear in 5 playlists (i.e., 41 tracks are tied for the most playlists).
- Examples of tracks with that maximum (5 playlists) include:
  - TrackId 3481 — A Midsummer Night's Dream, Op.61 Incidental Music: No.7 Notturno
  - TrackId 3408 — Aria Mit 30 Veränderungen, BWV 988 "Goldberg Variations": Aria
  - TrackId 3416 — Ave Maria
  - TrackId 3447 — Carmen: Overture
  - TrackId 3426 — Carmina Burana: O Fortuna
  (These are 5 of the 41 tied tracks. If you want the full list of all 41 track names and IDs, I can provide it.)

SQL I ran:
1) To list top tracks by playlist count (first 50 shown):
SELECT pt.TrackId, t.Name, COUNT(pt.PlaylistId) AS playlist_count
FROM PlaylistTrack pt
JOIN Track t USING(TrackId)
GROUP BY pt.TrackId, t.Name
ORDER BY playlist_count DESC, t.Name
LIMIT 50;

2) To get the maximum playlist count:
SELECT MAX(playlist_count) AS max_playlists FROM (
  SELECT TrackId, COUNT(PlaylistId) AS playlist_count
  FROM PlaylistTrack
  GROUP BY TrackId
);

3) To count how many tracks hit that maximum:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS num_tracks_with_max
FROM (
  SELECT TrackId, COUNT(PlaylistId) AS playlist_count
  FROM PlaylistTrack
  GROUP BY TrackId
  HAVING playlist_count = 5
);

4) To show examples (first 10) of tracks that appear in 5 playlists:
SELECT TrackId, Name FROM Track WHERE TrackId IN (
  SELECT TrackId FROM PlaylistTrack GROUP BY TrackId HAVING COUNT(PlaylistId)=5
) ORDER BY Name LIMIT 10;

Assumptions:
- I interpreted "appear in the most playlists" as tracks with the largest count of distinct PlaylistId entries in PlaylistTrack.
